game-container-config.intro: Spot the fatal line in each configuration.

challenges.q: docker run -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock image. Why fatal?
a: The Docker API lets you start a container mounting the host filesystem
challenges.why: Full API access is effectively root on the host.

challenges.q: privileged: true in a compose file. Impact?
a: All capabilities and device access, isolation effectively disabled
challenges.why: Privileged removes essentially every containment boundary.

challenges.q: Image runs as root inside the container and mounts the host /etc. Impact?
a: Writable host files, direct path to host compromise
challenges.why: Host mounts plus root inside is a documented escape path.

challenges.q: Which is the strongest hardening step for a web container?
a: Non-root user, dropped capabilities, read-only root filesystem
challenges.why: Least privilege inside limits what any escape is worth.

challenges.q: A container holds CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Why concerning?
a: It permits mounting filesystems and many privileged operations
challenges.why: CAP_SYS_ADMIN is a very broad capability and a common escape ingredient.

challenges.q: Kubernetes secret is stored in a Secret object. Is it encrypted by default?
a: No, base64-encoded unless encryption at rest is explicitly configured
challenges.why: Base64 is encoding, and RBAC is the only barrier by default.

challenges.q: Which Kubernetes permission most directly enables host compromise?
challenges.why: Creating a pod allows mounting host paths, privileged mode or host networking.

challenges.q: A pod mounts the hostPath / . Impact?
a: Direct access to the host filesystem, which is a full escape
challenges.why: The host root inside a container is compromise in one step.

game-rbac-path.intro: From this service account, reach cluster admin. Sequence the steps.

challenges.q: Order an RBAC escalation chain given create pods permission.
items: Read the service account token from the mounted path
Enumerate what the token can do with can-i
Create a pod that mounts the host filesystem
Read or modify the host to escalate
challenges.why: Token, enumerate, abuse the strongest permission, then escalate on the host.

challenges.q: You have get and list on secrets in one namespace, and a pod there uses a privileged service account. Order the chain.
items: Find a token or credential for a more privileged identity
Use it to enumerate further permissions
challenges.why: Secret access yields credentials, which yield permissions, which yield escalation.

challenges.q: Which single permission is most dangerous?
challenges.why: Creating a role binding lets you grant yourself any role, including cluster-admin.

challenges.q: Order the cloud chain from a vulnerable web app to cloud credentials.
items: Exploit SSRF in the web application
Call the cloud API as the instance role
challenges.why: SSRF to metadata to temporary credentials to cloud API is the standard cloud pivot.

challenges.q: Which is the correct first hardening step for a cluster?
items: Disable anonymous authentication and audit RBAC bindings
challenges.why: Un authenticated API access and over-broad bindings are the root of most cluster compromise.

game-iam-escalate.intro: Given the policy set, find the permission that grants more.

challenges.q: Policy grants iam:CreateAccessKey on *. What does this enable?
a: Creating a permanent credential for any user, including admins
challenges.why: Creating an access key for a privileged identity is direct escalation.

challenges.q: Policy grants iam:PassRole and lambda:CreateFunction. Impact?
a: Create a function running as a powerful role and invoke it
challenges.why: PassRole plus compute creation is a well-known escalation pair.

challenges.q: Policy grants s3:* on *. Worst case?
a: Full control of every bucket including deletion and policy changes
challenges.why: Wildcard action on wildcard resource is all buckets.

challenges.q: Policy grants sts:AssumeRole on *. Impact?
a: Assume any role in the account, potentially administrator
challenges.why: Unrestricted role assumption reaches whatever the most privileged role can do.

challenges.q: Which is a safer pattern than a long-lived access key?
a: Storing it in the repo encrypted
challenges.why: Temporary credentials bound exposure in time.

challenges.q: What is the primary defence against credential exposure in cloud?
a: Least privilege roles with short-lived credentials and monitoring of identity events
challenges.why: Identity is the perimeter, so identity controls and monitoring are the defence.

challenges.q: An instance metadata endpoint returns credentials without a token header. Why is this dangerous?
a: Any SSRF can retrieve cloud credentials directly
challenges.why: It converts a web bug into a cloud account compromise.
